title: Reads on concatenated words
statement: Let $c:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$, let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$, and let $a,b$ be finite Boolean words. Suppose that for every natural number $r$ less than the length of $a$ concatenated with $b$, the cell at position $p+r$ contains the $r$-th bit of that concatenation. Then every position $p+r$ for $r$ within $a$ contains the corresponding bit of $a$, and every position $p+|a|+r$ for $r$ within $b$ contains the corresponding bit of $b$.
hypotheses_covered: Cell-content function c from integers to optional bits
Finite Boolean words a and b
Every in-range cell of the concatenation contains its corresponding bit
